value: Light regime alters seed germination during salt exposure; responses depend on the saline treatment.
method: Controlled seed-germination experiment; binomial generalized linear models of germination percentages at 14, 21 and 30 days.
conditions: 12 h light-dark regime versus continuous darkness; NaCl, KCl, CaCl2, MgCl2 and an equimolar salt mixture, 0–360 mM.

source.authors: Cordovilla MDP, Sánchez I, Aguilar MG, Melendo M
source.title: Chloride Salts and Light Modulate Germination and Early Seedling Performance in Dittrichia viscosa

quote: Both the light regime and light regime × saline treatment interaction significantly affected FGP14, FGP21, and FGP30, indicating that the response during salt exposure depended on light conditions.
note: Full text read. This is a nonvisual seed-germination response to illumination, not evidence of a particular photoreceptor or an endogenous diel rhythm. Salt-free final germination did not differ significantly between light regimes.
